evidence.field: 包 entry; pronunciation line and attributed received-form analysis
evidence.text: The printed 包 headword gives bāo. Zhou Baohong calls 包 a 会意字, reading 勹 as wrapping, 巳 as an unborn child, and their combination as conveying 胞衣. He presents this as his account of the received form, not an independently verified origin. The entry also proposes that 包 should have existed in Western Zhou based on its use in the Shijing, while stating that it is not found in Shang or Western Zhou writing in his account. This is an attributed dating proposal, not an independently verified artifact attestation.
evidence.title: 字源 (2012)

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 包 entry; received 說文 forms, readings, and senses
evidence.text: The entry reproduces separate received 說文 explanations: 包 as a pregnant figure with 巳 inside representing an unformed child, and 勹 as a bent figure enclosing something. Both are assigned 布交切. It lists pregnancy separately from containing/enclosing senses and cites 詩經·召南·野有死麇, 白茅包之. This documents the dictionary tradition and a transmitted wrapping example, but does not establish an early graphic origin or date the quotation’s written witness.
evidence.title: [A00408] 包 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: China National Museum of Chinese Writing, 《说抱、包》内容概述, reporting Xie Mingwen’s proposal
evidence.field: Lines 72–73; competing interpretation of oracle-bone graphs and proposed 包 descent
evidence.text: The museum summary reports Xie Mingwen’s argument that graphs in Heji 16429 and 26986, conventionally read as 保, instead depict a child held in front of a person. He proposes that this graph developed into 包, which first wrote 抱. The summary contrasts this proposal with the received-form analysis 从巳、勹声 and the Shuowen pregnancy account. It does not establish the reading or proposed descent with dated intermediate forms.
evidence.title: 《说抱、包》内容概述 - 中国文字博物馆

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 包 entry; Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) values reported in its reconstruction and phonetic-series tables
evidence.field: Glyph origin, Zhengzhang series, and Old Chinese reconstruction table
evidence.text: The entry identifies 勹 as the phonetic component in its Zhengzhang table and lists 勹 and 包 with Old Chinese *pruː. It separately reports 包 as *pˁ<r>u in Baxter–Sagart system 1.1. These are reconstruction values reported by a compilation, not recorded ancient pronunciations; the paired Zhengzhang values support a sound comparison but do not prove 勹’s role in the earliest formation.
